## Projects Department Health & Safety Standards

Ref:EGY/PRJCTS/HSE/REQs

- The crane and carrier should be inspected every day by a competent person. The crane and associated equipment should be suitably de-rated and the crane should be operated in accordance with the recommendations inBs7121Part1-5 andPart13 Codeof Practice forSafeUse of Cranes.
- For all crane types,whether they lift personnel or other materials,independent third party inspections of the crane and related equipment must be completed and documented by a competent person in line with the highest requirements and frequencies as defined within the crane manufacturers, legislative, and/or recognized Standard.
- Additionally,for all crane types,whether theylift personnel or other materials,the crane operator must have evidence on their person at all timesthat theyare demonstrably competent to operate the specific crane in use.

## 3.12.9. Fall Protection Systems

- > The use of personal fall protection systems are only to be used to prevent or minimize the consequences of a fall when collective preventative measures (i.e. scaffold, MEWP etc.) are not reasonablypracticable.
- There are several types of personal fall protection systems, however the main two likely to be used across the program are fall restraint and fall arrest systems.
- Fall restraint systems prevent a person from physically getting to a place where they could fall whereas a fall arrest system only limits the height or consequences ofa fall. Therefore the use of fall restraint is to be given a higher priority over fall arrest when planning and implementing fall protection systems.
- Workers who set and use fall protection systems are to be adequately trained and competent and are to be closely supervised.
- A rescue plan showing how a person(s) will be recovered in the event of a fall is to be included in method statements.
- Rescue operation is to be carried out and supervised by competent persons.
- Enforcement actionwillbe taken where rescue plans have notbeen provided or found to be inadequate

## 3.12.10.Safety Harnesses and Lanyards

- Before the use of safety harnesses are authorized, those managing the works are to ensure that no othermeansoffallprotectionis available.
- Where a safety harness is to be worn it is to be a full body harness and fitted with an energy absorbing lanyard (in the case of fall arrest) unless the situation dictates otherwise.The use of safety belts is prohibited.
- Safety lanyards/harnesses must be worn and attached when working at a height of over 2m and there is a risk of a fall.
- A Where the working height is under 6m or within aMEWP the shock absorber must be disengaged or clippedbackonitself.
